# nagios_user (Resource)

Manages a Nagios XI login/admin panel user account (system/user) - distinct from a monitoring nagios_contact, which only receives alerts and has no login capability. Note: Nagios's API has no server-side filter by username for this object type, so every lookup (Create's post-write confirmation, every Read/Update, and the nagios_user data source) fetches the entire unfiltered user list; this is expected to be low-cost for the small, admin-managed set of XI panel accounts most deployments have, but may be noticeably slower with a very large number of users.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Local account example. password/auth_level/force_pw_change/auth_type/
# auth_server_id are all write-only - Nagios never returns them from a GET,
# so changing them outside Terraform isn't detected as drift. In practice
# password should come from a secret source, not a literal in configuration.
resource "nagios_user" "local_admin" {
  username        = "jdoe"
  name            = "Jane Doe"
  email           = "jdoe@example.com"
  password        = "change-me"
  auth_level      = "admin"
  force_pw_change = true
  auth_type       = "local"
}

# SSO/LDAP-linked example - requires a valid auth_server_id referencing an
# existing nagios_authserver.
resource "nagios_authserver" "corp_ldap" {
  enabled           = true
  connection_method = "ldap"
  ldap_host         = "ldap.example.com"
  ldap_port         = "389"
  base_dn           = "DC=example,DC=com"
  security_level    = "tls"
}

resource "nagios_user" "sso_user" {
  username       = "asmith"
  name           = "Alice Smith"
  email          = "asmith@example.com"
  password       = "change-me"
  auth_level     = "user"
  auth_type      = "sso"
  auth_server_id = nagios_authserver.corp_ldap.server_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `auth_level` (String) The user's permission level, either "user" or "admin". Write-only, see "password"
- `email` (String) The user's email address. Nagios requires a valid value here on every update, even when only unrelated fields are changing
- `name` (String) The user's full name
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The user's password. Write-only: Nagios never returns this from a GET, so it is not detected as drifted if changed outside Terraform - only an explicit config change is applied
- `username` (String) The login username. Mutable - Nagios supports renaming an existing user in place

### Optional

- `auth_server_id` (String) The nagios_authserver.server_id this user authenticates against. Required when auth_type is "sso". Write-only, see "password"
- `auth_type` (String) Either "local" for a standalone account with its own password, or "sso" for one authenticated via an existing nagios_authserver (see auth_server_id). Write-only, see "password"
- `enabled` (Boolean) Determines whether or not this user account is enabled
- `force_pw_change` (Boolean) Forces the user to change their password at next login. Write-only, see "password"

### Read-Only

- `user_id` (String) The ID of the user. This value is computed by Nagios

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Users are imported by username. password/auth_level/force_pw_change/
# auth_type/auth_server_id can never be read back from Nagios (#174) and
# will be unknown after import until set explicitly in configuration.
terraform import nagios_user.jdoe jdoe
```
